questions.question: A sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice. How much a month are you paid?
questions.questionHtml:
A sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice.

How much a month are you paid?

options.text: How much a month do you pay?
options.html: How much a month do you pay?

options.text: How much a month do you pay them?
options.html: How much a month do you pay them?

options.text: How much a month do they pay you?
options.html: How much a month do they pay you?

options.text: In a month how much do you pay?
options.html: In a month how much do you pay?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3) i.e. How much a month do they pay you?

 

  • In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes subject performing an action.
  • In Passive Voice, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
  • The given sentence is in the passive voice.
  • When we convert this sentence into active voice, the invisible subject 'they' should be included in the sentence.
  • The passive format "are + V3" is used in the given sentence.
  • This is the active and passive voice rule for the present simple tense. Thus, the present simple tense of active voice should be used.
  • Hence, "How much a month do they pay you?" is the correct active voice.


 

  • Verbs of passive format have a different set of tenses (*V3 - Past participle or Third form of the Verb) as given below in the table:
     
    TENSE ACTIVE PASSIVE PASSIVE CONVERSION
    Present Simple He plays football am/is/are + V3 Football is played by him
    Present Continuous He is playing football am/is/are + being +V3 Football is being played by him
    Present Perfect He has played football Has/have + been+ V3 Football has been played by him
    Present Perfect Continuous He has been playing football Not used and unusual. Not used and unusual
    Past Simple He played football Was/were + V3 Football was played by him
    Past Continuous He was playing football Was/were + being + V3 Football was being played by him
    Past Perfect He had played football Had + been + V3 Football had been played by him
    Past Perfect Continuous He had been playing football Not used and unusual Not used and unusual
    Future Simple He will play football Will + be + V3 Football will be played by him
    Future Continuous He will be playing football Not used and unusual Not used and unusual
    Future Perfect He will have played football Will have been + V3 Football will have been played by him
    Future Perfect Continuous He will have been playing football Not used and unusual Not used and unusual

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. Lavanya was happy to see that the tree they had planted the previous year has grow quite taller.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

Lavanya was happy to see that the tree they had planted the previous year has grow quite taller.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'had grown quite tall'.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
  • Here, 'had grown quite tall' should be used instead of 'has grown quite taller'.
  • The given sentence is in the past perfect tense. Hence, the use of present tense is grammatically incorrect.
  • We need to follow the rule of parallelism as the subject 'Lavanya' is common in the whole sentence, so the same tense shall be used to make it grammatically correct.
  • We tend to go for Option 4 but it would be incorrect because 'a superlative adjective is an adjective used in comparisons to describe something as being of the highest degree or extreme'. 
  • Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is Option 1.
     

Correct Sentence: Lavanya was happy to see that the tree they had planted the previous year had grown quite tall.

Hinglish

  • दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से गलत है।
  • यहां 'has grow quite taller' के बजाय 'had grown quite tall' का इस्तेमाल किया जाना चाहिए।
  • दिया गया वाक्य Past perfect  Tense में है। इसलिए, Present Tense का उपयोग व्याकरणिक रूप से गलत है।
  • हमें समानता के नियम का पालन करने की आवश्यकता है क्योंकि 'लावण्य' विषय पूरे वाक्य में सामान्य है, इसलिए इसे व्याकरणिक रूप से सही बनाने के लिए उसी काल का उपयोग किया जाएगा।
  • हम विकल्प 4 के लिए जाते हैं लेकिन यह गलत होगा क्योंकि 'एक Superlative Adjective एक Adjective है जिसका उपयोग किसी चीज को उच्चतम डिग्री या चरम के रूप में वर्णित करने के लिए किया जाता है'।
  • इसलिए, ऊपर वर्णित बिंदुओं के अनुसार, हम पाते हैं कि सही उत्तर विकल्प 1 है।

questions.question: Given below are four sentences in jumbled order. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. He seemed to remain that high for nearly two years. B. Kari, the elephant was five months old when he was given to me to take care of. C. We grew together, that is probably why I never found out just how tall he was. D. I was nine years old and I could reach his back if I stood on tiptoe.
questions.questionHtml:
Given below are four sentences in jumbled order. Select the option that gives their correct order.

A. He seemed to remain that high for nearly two years.

B. Kari, the elephant was five months old when he was given to me to take care of.

C. We grew together, that is probably why I never found out just how tall he was.

D. I was nine years old and I could reach his back if I stood on tiptoe.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'BDAC'.

Key Points

  • The given question is an example of a Para Jumble.
  • We know that the first statement of a para jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, starting off a story, starting of an incident or an event, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'.
  • Sentence B will be the starting line because it contains the main idea of the para jumble i.e. Kari, the elephant.
  • However, Sentence D states that the narrator was nine years old when the elephant was given to him to take care of. He could reach his back if he stood on tiptoe.
  • So, D will follow B.
  • Sentence A will be next because it mentions 'that high' which corresponds to the height of the elephant mentioned in sentence D.
  • So, C will follow A because it tells why the narrator never found out how tall Kari was.
  • Thus, the correct sequence is:
    • B: Kari, the elephant was five months old when he was given to me to take care of.
    • D: I was nine years old and I could reach his back if I stood on tiptoe.
    • A: He seemed to remain that high for nearly two years.
    • C: We grew together, that is probably why I never found out just how tall he was.
       

Correct Sequence: Kari, the elephant was five months old when he was given to me to take care of. I was nine years old and I could reach his back if I stood on tiptoe. He seemed to remain that high for nearly two years. We grew together, that is probably why I never found out just how tall he was.

questions.question: Direction: Select the grammatically correct form of the given sentence from the following options. Many people are use the internet for booking tickets these days.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Select the grammatically correct form of the given sentence from the following options.

Many people are use the internet for booking tickets these days.

options.text: Many people are having used the internet for booking tickets these days.
options.html: Many people are having used the internet for booking tickets these days.

options.text: Many people are being using the internet for booking tickets these days.
options.html: Many people are being using the internet for booking tickets these days.

options.text: Many people are using the internet for booking tickets these days.
options.html: Many people are using the internet for booking tickets these days.

options.text: Many people was using the internet for booking tickets these days.
options.html: Many people was using the internet for booking tickets these days.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '​Many people are using the internet for booking tickets these days.' 

Key Points

  • In this sentence, we are talking about the continuous use of the internet for booking tickets.
  • Therefore, we need to write the sentence in the Present Continuous Tense.
  • The present continuous tense is used to describe dynamic actions that happen repeatedly, are currently happening, or will be happening in the near future.
  • Structure:
    • Subject + is/am/are + V1 + ing + object.
      • Example: Boys are playing cricket in the garden area.
         

Correct sentence: Many people are using the internet for booking tickets these days.
 

Additional Information    

  • The present progressive tense is used to indicate the ongoing time (now).
  • However, the stative verbs do not usually take the form of present progressive tense even though they refer to the present time.
  • Now, continually, perpetually, at this moment, at the moment, right now, this season, this year, forever, etc. words or word pairs are usually signs that the verb in a sentence is in the present progressive form.
  • However, these signs are not necessary all the time for a verb to be of present progressive tense.

questions.question: "I shall never forget the help I got from my parents. They have been so generous all through my days in school and college." Report this as told by a male person.
questions.questionHtml: "I shall never forget the help I got from my parents. They have been so generous all through my days in school and college." Report this as told by a male person.

options.text: He said that he shall never forget the help he got from his parents. He has been so generous all through their days in school and college.
options.html: He said that he shall never forget the help he got from his parents. He has been so generous all through their days in school and college.

options.text: He said that he would never forget the help he had got from his parents. He added that they had been so generous all through his days in school and college.
options.html: He said that he would never forget the help he had got from his parents. He added that they had been so generous all through his days in school and college.

options.text: They said that he would never forget the help he had got from his parents. They added that he had been so generous all through their days in school and college
options.html: They said that he would never forget the help he had got from his parents. They added that he had been so generous all through their days in school and college

options.text: She said that she would never forget the help she had got from her parents. She added that they had been so generous all through her days in school and college.
options.html: She said that she would never forget the help she had got from her parents. She added that they had been so generous all through her days in school and college.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'He said that he would never forget the help he had got from his parents. He added that they had been so generous all through his days in school and college'.

Key Points

  • We have to write the given speech as told by a male person hence, we will use 'he' as a pronoun.
  • We will write 'he said that' at the starting of the sentence and convert the direct speech into indirect speech.
  • In indirect speech 'shall' will convert into 'would'.
  • 'From my parents' will convert into 'from his parents'.
  • To start the next sentence we will add -  'He added that' to mention the next point.
  • 'Have been' will change into 'had been'.
  • 'My days in school and college' will change into 'his days in school and college'.

Hence the indirect speech will be made as - He said that he would never forget the help he had got from his parents. He added that they had been so generous all through his days in school and college'.

questions.question: Directions: A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested below, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice. Nobody has answered my question.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested below, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.

Nobody has answered my question.

options.text: My question has been answered by somebody.
options.html: My question has been answered by somebody.

options.text: My question has not been answered by anybody.
options.html: My question has not been  answered by anybody.
My question was not answered.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "My question has not been  answered by anybody."

Key Points

  • The given sentence is "Nobody has answered my question," which is in the active voice.
  • The structure for the active voice sentence is: Subject + has/have + past participle + object
  • In the given sentence:
    • "Nobody" is the subject.
    • "Has answered" is the verb in the present perfect tense.
    • "My question" is the object.
  • To convert this sentence into passive voice, we switch the positions of the subject and object, and adjust the form of the verb as per the guidance.
  • The verb is in the present perfect tense, so the passive form also needs to stay in the present perfect tense.
  • The structure for the passive voice is: Object + has/have + been + past participle + by + agent
  • Looking at the alternatives:
    • "My question has been answered by somebody." - This sentence is incorrect because the word 'somebody' contradicts the initial statement suggesting 'nobody' has answered the question.
    • "My question has not been answered by anybody." - This maintains the tense (present perfect) and the meaning and it's in correct structure.
    • "My question was not answered." - While this sentence maintains the same meaning, it changes the tense from the present perfect to the simple past.
    • "My question remains unanswered." - This sentence also maintains the same meaning, but it changes the verb tense to simple present.
  • Therefore, "My question has not been answered by anybody," correctly translates the sentence into passive voice while maintaining the original tense and meaning.

Thus, the correct answer is "Option 2".

questions.question: Choose the word that means the same as the given word. Abbreviate
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Abbreviate
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Curtail.

Key Points

  • The word "Abbreviate" means to shorten something, particularly a word or phrase. It refers to making something briefer or more concise. (संक्षेपित करना)
    • Example: "Dr." is the abbreviated form of "Doctor."
  • "Curtail" means to reduce or limit something, particularly in size or extent. It implies shortening or cutting short. (कम करना)
    • Example: Due to budget cuts, the company had to curtail its marketing expenses.
  • Hence, we can infer that the synonym of 'Abbreviate' is 'Curtail' as both refer to making something shorter or reduced in size.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Curtail.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Dilate (विस्तार करना): To make something larger, wider, or more expansive in scope.
    • Example: The doctor asked me to dilate my eyes for the eye exam.
  • Sycophant (चापलूस): A person who acts excessively obedient or servile towards someone in power to gain favor.
    • Example: The CEO was surrounded by sycophants who constantly praised him.
  • Dilute (पतला करना): To make a substance weaker by adding water or another liquid.
    • Example: You should dilute the juice with some water, as it's too sweet.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech. He said that when Ram was enjoying, Shyam was studying.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

He said that when Ram was enjoying, Shyam was studying.

options.text: He said, "When Ram was being enjoyed, Shyam was being studied".
options.html: He said, "When Ram was being enjoyed, Shyam was being studied".

options.text: He said, "When Ram would enjoying, Shyam would studying".
options.html: He said, "When Ram would enjoying, Shyam would studying".

options.text: He says, "When Ram is enjoying, then Shyam must be studying".
options.html: He says, "When Ram is enjoying, then Shyam must be studying".

options.text: He said, "When Ram was enjoying, Shyam was studying".
options.html: He said, "When Ram was enjoying, Shyam was studying".

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: He said, "When Ram was enjoying, Shyam was studying".

Key Points

  • The given sentence is in indirect speech, and we need to convert it to direct speech.
  • When we change an indirect speech to direct speech, we must follow these rules:
    • The reporting verb 'said' remains unchanged.
    • The conjunction 'that' is replaced with inverted commas ("...") to show the direct speech part.
    • A comma (,) is added after the direct speech part.
    • The first word of the direct speech is in capital letters.
    • The Past indefinite tense or the Past continuous tense is not changed if the reported speech states two actions that took place at the same time.
  • Thus, option 4 is the correct answer.
     

Hence, direct speech is- He said, "When Ram was enjoying, Shyam was studying".

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. The detective went the whole nine yards in his investigation.

questions.question: Choose the most appropriate antonym of the underlined word. But he was so profligate in his morals that his name cannot be mentioned with anything like tolerance.
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the most appropriate antonym of the underlined word.

But he was so profligate in his morals that his name cannot be mentioned with anything like tolerance.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1.

Key Points

  • The word "profligate" means recklessly extravagant or wasteful in the use of resources; having low moral standards. (बदचलन)
    • Example: His profligate spending habits left him penniless within a year.
  • "Conserve" refers to the act of protecting something from harm or destruction, especially resources. (संरक्षण करना)
    • Example: We must conserve water to ensure we have enough for future generations.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'profligate' is 'conserve'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Wild (जंगली): Living or growing in the natural environment; not domesticated or cultivated.
    • Example: The wild animals roamed freely across the plains.
  • Liberal (उदार): Open to new behavior or opinions and willing to discard traditional values.
    • Example: She has liberal views on education and believes in progressive teaching methods.
  • Lewd (अश्लील): Crude and offensive in a sexual way.
    • Example: The comedian's lewd jokes were not appreciated by everyone in the audience.

questions.question: What will come in blank (1)?
questions.questionHtml: What will come in blank (1)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Fillip'.
 
Key Points
  • The passage discusses the "Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes," which are government initiatives designed to boost or stimulate specific industrial sectors.
  • "Fillip" (प्रोत्साहन/बढ़ावा) refers to something that acts as a stimulus or a boost to an activity. In the context of economic policy, PLI schemes serve as a financial fillip to encourage domestic production.
  • "Hindrance" (बाधा) is the opposite of a boost; it means something that provides resistance or delay.
  • "Quagmire" (नाज़ुक स्थिति/दलदल) refers to a complex or hazardous situation that is difficult to escape. While the broader industrial landscape is described as a quagmire later in the sentence, the PLI schemes themselves are positive stimuli.
  • "Shibboleth" (पुरानी घिसी-पिटी धारणा) is a belief or custom that is no longer important or relevant. This does not fit the description of an active economic incentive.
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 2'.
Complete Passage: India’s aspiration to catalyze a manufacturing renaissance is often described as a daring attempt to bypass the traditional "Lewisian" transition from agriculture to industry, leaping straight into a high-value service economy that now requires a physical backbone. While the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes have provided a much-needed (1) Fillip to specific sectors like mobile telephony and pharmaceuticals, the broader industrial landscape remains a (2) __________ of archaic labor laws and logistical inefficiencies that inflate the "cost of doing business." It is vital that the executive branch (3) __________ comprehensive land reforms and bureaucratic streamlining, as the current difficulty in land acquisition remains the primary deterrent for "greenfield" investments by global multi-nationals. This structural rigidity often traps smaller enterprises in a cycle of low productivity, preventing them from scaling up and integrating into global value chains. Furthermore, the persistent gap between academic curricula and industry requirements exacerbates the problem, leaving a vast portion of the workforce under-equipped for high-precision roles.

Moreover, neither the lucrative incentives for high-tech fabrication (4) __________ the rhetoric of "Atmanirbharta" have been able to mask the (5) __________ of indigenous research and development spending, which remains stagnated at less than 1% of GDP compared to the global average. This lack of "deep-tech" investment ensures that India remains at the lower end of the value chain, focused on assembly rather than innovation, which limits the potential for long-term wealth creation. Without a drastic increase in private sector participation in innovation, the goal of becoming a global manufacturing powerhouse may remain elusive. Ultimately, the success of the "Make in India" initiative depends on whether the state can move beyond creating a mere simulacrum of efficiency and instead address the deep-seated structural bottlenecks that stifle the entrepreneurial spirit.

 
Additional Information
  • Lewisian Transition: An economic theory where surplus labor moves from the traditional agricultural sector to the modern industrial sector, fueling growth.
  • Greenfield Investment: A type of foreign direct investment (FDI) where a parent company creates a new venture in a foreign country by constructing new operational facilities from the ground up.
  • Catalyze: To cause or accelerate a reaction or change.

The correct answer is 'prioritize'.
 
Key Points
  • The sentence starts with the anticipatory structure "It is vital that...". In high-level English, adjectives denoting importance or necessity (like vital, essential, imperative, crucial) trigger the mandative subjunctive mood.
  • In a "that" clause following these triggers, the verb must be in its base form (the infinitive without 'to'), which is "prioritize".
  • This base form remains unchanged regardless of the subject. Even though "the executive branch" is a singular subject, you do not add an '-s' (prioritizes) in the subjunctive mood.
  • Option 2 ("to prioritize") is an infinitive and Option 4 ("prioritizing") is a gerund/participle; neither can serve as the finite verb in this specific clause structure.
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 1'.

questions.question: What will come in blank (4)?
questions.questionHtml: What will come in blank (4)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'nor has'.
 
Key Points
  • The sentence begins with the negative correlative conjunction "neither" ("Moreover, neither the lucrative incentives...").
  • In English grammar, "neither" must be paired with "nor" to join two negative options or subjects. This is a Correlative Conjunction pair.
  • The subject following "nor" is "the rhetoric of Atmanirbharta," which is singular. Therefore, the singular auxiliary verb "has" is required to complete the present perfect construction ("...nor has the rhetoric... been able to mask").
  • Option 1 ("and has") and Option 3 ("but has") are logically and grammatically incorrect when paired with "neither."
  • Option 2 ("or has") is the correct partner for "either," not "neither."
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 4'.

It is vital that the executive branch (3) prioritize comprehensive land reforms and bureaucratic streamlining, as the current difficulty in land acquisition remains the primary deterrent for "greenfield" investments by global multi-nationals. This structural rigidity often traps smaller enterprises in a cycle of low productivity, preventing them from scaling up and integrating into global value chains. Furthermore, the persistent gap between academic curricula and industry requirements exacerbates the problem, leaving a vast portion of the workforce under-equipped for high-precision roles.

Moreover, neither the lucrative incentives for high-tech fabrication (4) nor has the rhetoric of "Atmanirbharta" have been able to mask the (5) __________ of indigenous research and development spending, which remains stagnated at less than 1% of GDP compared to the global average. This lack of "deep-tech" investment ensures that India remains at the lower end of the value chain, focused on assembly rather than innovation, which limits the potential for long-term wealth creation. Without a drastic increase in private sector participation in innovation, the goal of becoming a global manufacturing powerhouse may remain elusive. Ultimately, the success of the "Make in India" initiative depends on whether the state can move beyond creating a mere simulacrum of efficiency and instead address the deep-seated structural bottlenecks that stifle the entrepreneurial spirit.

 
Additional Information
  • Subject-Verb Agreement with Neither/Nor: When two subjects are joined by "neither/nor," the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. In this case, "rhetoric" (singular) is closer than "incentives" (plural), so we use "has."
  • Atmanirbharta (आत्मनिर्भरता): Self-reliance. In the context of Indian policy, it refers to reducing dependence on imports by strengthening domestic manufacturing.
  • Lucrative (लाभप्रद): Producing a great deal of profit.

Key Points
  • The passage notes that research and development (R&D) spending in India "remains stagnated at less than 1% of GDP compared to the global average." This indicates an insufficient amount.

  • "Plethora" (बहुतायत) and "Surfeit" (अधिकता) both mean an excessive amount or a surplus. These are the opposite of what the context (less than 1%) requires.
  • "Vicissitudes" (उतार-चढ़ाव) refers to a change of circumstances or fortune, typically one that is unwelcome or unpleasant. While R&D spending might face ups and downs, the sentence specifically targets the lack of spending that is being "masked."
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 3'.
